newsitem.title: USA: Adelphia, Time Warner in cable swap.
newsitem.headline: Adelphia, Time Warner in cable swap.

text.p: Adelphia Communications Corp said Tuesday it has struck a deal to trade cable television systems in seven states with Time Warner cable companies.

The deal, involving the swap of about 250,000 cable subscribers, also includes an exchange of interests in four local telephone networks in New York state and an undisclosed amount of cash, the company said.
Adelphia said it will trade systems in Mansfield, Ohio, for Time Warner systems in New York, Virginia and New England that are adjacent to existing Adelphia systems.
Adelphia said its affiliates in Syracuse, N.Y., and Henderson, N.C., will turn over those systems to Time Warner in exchange for systems in western Pennsylvania and Virginia.

Adelphia said its Hyperion Telecommunications unit will trade interests in four local telephone networks in upstate New York. Hyperion will receive a 50 percent interest in the Buffalo network and a 100 percent interest in the Syracuse network while handing over all interests in the Albany and Binghamton networks to Time Warner, it said.
Adelphia said it will have 273,000 customers in Virginia, 223,000 in western Pennsylvania, and 234,000 in New England.
